# T1. First Optimization & Judge Loop

<!-- section:scenario -->
> **Optional Tutorial (excluded from the 0/100 score)**: Skip anytime from the exercise list or head straight to **#001**.

Let's test running the solver and reading the judge feedback!

A bakery makes **croissants** (`croissants >= 0`) and **loaves** (`loaves >= 0`) using flour and butter. Everything in the starter code is already written **except one deliberate bug**: it calls `minimize(...)` instead of maximizing profit.

1. Click **Run & Judge** right away to see the yellow **SUBOPTIMAL** feedback (making 0 of everything yields `0` profit!).
2. Fix that single word (`minimize` -> `maximize`, and `h.minimize(...)` -> `h.maximize(...)` in the Python tab) and run again to earn **AC**.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input**: `flourCap`, `butterCap`, unit profits (`croissantProfit`, `loafProfit`), and resource usage per unit (`croissantFlour`, `croissantButter`, `loafFlour`, `loafButter`).
- **Output**: `{ croissants: number, loaves: number, totalProfit: number }`

<!-- section:example -->
With `flourCap = 120`, `butterCap = 70`, croissants yielding `40` (using 2 flour, 1 butter) and loaves yielding `70` (using 3 flour, 2 butter), baking `croissants = 30`, `loaves = 20` uses all `120` flour and `70` butter for optimal profit **`2600`**.

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Look for `m.objective(minimize(...))` in **WaSHI (TypeScript)** or `h.minimize(...)` in **Python (highspy)**. Both libraries expose `maximize` as well.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Why did the broken code say **SUBOPTIMAL** instead of **VIOLATION**? Because producing `(0, 0)` violates no capacity limits — it is feasible, just far from the maximum profit! Distinguishing **feasible-but-suboptimal** from **infeasible/violated** is your most useful debugging signal in mathematical optimization.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max \quad & p_c c + p_l \ell \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & f_c c + f_l \ell \le F_{\text{cap}} \\
& b_c c + b_l \ell \le B_{\text{cap}} \\
& c, \ell \ge 0
\end{aligned}
$$

judge.m0: Output must be an object { croissants, loaves, totalProfit }.
judge.m1: Production quantities cannot be negative (got croissants={p0}, loaves={p1}).
judge.m4: Reported totalProfit ({p0}) does not match profit from quantities ({p1}).
judge.m5: Feasible schedule, but total profit ({p0}) is below optimal ({p1}). Check your objective sense!
